interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 7.8 and an ISUP grade group 3 identified on the prostatectomy specimen (Gleason 4+3). Countervailing findings include no extraprostatic extension, absence of seminal vesicle invasion, and negative lymphovascular invasion. The surgical margins were positive, which is a noted risk factor. Biopsy-to-prostatectomy differences are present; the biopsy showed an ISUP grade group 2, while the prostatectomy specimen was ISUP grade group 3. Nodal status was assessed, showing no metastasis. Missing postoperative PSA and follow-up information limits prognostic certainty regarding future trajectory. The prognosis would be significantly revised with subsequent postoperative PSA measurements and their documented pattern of change over time. The fixed estimated horizon is 56.82 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 42.61–71.02 months; its coverage has not been validated.

Positive surgical margins are concerning findings. Countervailing points include no documented extraprostatic extension, absence of seminal vesicle invasion, and lack of lymphovascular invasion or node metastasis. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference shows a lower grade group (ISUP 2) at biopsy versus ISUP 3 post-surgery. Nodal status was assessed with no metastasis noted. Information regarding the postoperative PSA trajectory would significantly revise this prognosis.
